samples.summary: Subtest "via the merge ref's first parent" cannot fail if mergeRefBaseTip is broken — the assertion holds via the baseBranchTip fallback
samples.evidence: The subtest builds HEAD at a two-parent merge and asserts `refs.base === freshBase` (line 512) and `changedPaths(refs, tmp) === ["feature.txt"]`. But in that fixture `main` still points at `freshBase`, so `baseBranchTip(git, "main", ...)` returns the exact same sha (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:288-291 tries mergeRefBaseTip then baseBranchTip). Delete or break `mergeRefBaseTip` entirely and this subtest still passes — it is the only test named for that code path, so the merge-ref-first-parent logic (including the `parents.length !== 3` and `parents[2] !== headSha` guards at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:220-224) has no assertion that actually discriminates it. Isolating it would require hiding the `main`/`origin/main` refs, as subtest 3 does for the stale fallback.

samples.summary: The changed `push` branch of resolveRefs (head now `payload.after`, falling back to the literal "HEAD") has no test
samples.evidence: resolveRefs's push arm changed from returning a bare base to `{ base: verified(payload.before), head: verified(payload.after) ?? "HEAD" }`. Nothing exercises it: the only push-related test (scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:223) sets GITHUB_REF_NAME=main and short-circuits in `resolve` before resolveRefs is reached (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:530). No test writes a push payload with `before`/`after`, so neither the new `after` resolution, the silent "HEAD" fallback when `after` is absent/unfetched, nor the all-zeroes guard on the new shape is covered — an unverified `after` silently reverts to diffing the checkout, which is precisely the class of bug this PR is fixing for pull_request.

samples.summary: The new label-removal behavior in ci-report.yml is untested, even though the repo does structurally test workflow YAML
samples.evidence: The diff adds an `else if (areas)` branch calling `issues.removeLabel` with a 404-swallowing `.catch`, plus the new invariant that a missing `areas` must leave the label alone. Nothing asserts any of it: scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs only reads `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (line 20), and grep for `ci-report`/`removeLabel` across scripts/test finds no match. So the three-way behavior (add / remove / leave-alone-when-unresolved) and the 404-vs-rethrow distinction rest entirely on review.

samples.summary: baseBranchTip's ref sanitising and the origin/upstream preference order are untested
samples.evidence: `baseBranchTip` rejects base refs failing `/^[\w./-]+$/` and tries `origin/<ref>`, `upstream/<ref>`, `<ref>` in order. The tests only ever supply `ref: "main"` in a fixture with no remotes (scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:504), so the local-branch path is the only one exercised: a malformed/hostile `base.ref`, a missing `base.ref` (undefined), and the remote-tracking lookups (`refs/remotes/origin/main`) all have no assertion. A regression that dropped the regex or the remote prefixes would keep every test green.

samples.summary: The "'Update branch' re-resolves…" test bypasses the resolver it is named after
samples.evidence: The test's title and comment are about how resolution behaves after GitHub's "Update branch" (head.sha becomes a merge whose second parent is not head.sha, so mergeRefBaseTip must decline and baseBranchTip must supply the base). But the body never calls `resolveRefs`; it hand-picks `base`/`head` from git and calls `changedPaths` (line 449). So it verifies three-dot diff arithmetic — already covered by the test above it — and not the resolution path, including the `parents[2] !== headSha` guard that this scenario is the natural trigger for.
searchedFor: grep resolveRefs occurrences in the test file

samples.summary: merge_group only has a happy-path test; the new `base && head` fail-safe is unasserted
samples.evidence: The merge_group arm now returns null unless BOTH `base_sha` and `head_sha` verify (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:294-297). The test at line 623 asserts only the both-present case. No case with a missing/unfetched `head_sha` or `base_sha`, so a regression that fell back to "HEAD" (the merge-queue checkout) instead of failing safe would pass — the same class of bug the pull_request arm has an explicit test for (line 605).

verdict.reason: Verified against the repo. In the subtest at scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:507-514 the fixture leaves branch `main` pointing at `freshBase` (set at line 497; `git checkout -B merge-ref main` at line 509 does not move `main`), and the payload's `base.ref` is "main" (line 504). scripts/changed-areas.mjs:288-291 falls back from `mergeRefBaseTip` to `baseBranchTip`, whose last candidate is plain `main^{commit}` (line 244-246) — which resolves to the very same `freshBase` in this fixture, with no remotes present. Therefore `assert.equal(refs.base, freshBase)` (line 512) and `changedPaths(refs, tmp) === ["feature.txt"]` (line 513) both still hold if `mergeRefBaseTip` returns null (deleted, or with its `parents.length !== 3` / `parents[2] !== headSha` guards at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:220-224 removed or inverted). Subtest 2 (lines 516-523) already covers that same baseBranchTip route, and subtest 3 (lines 525-539) demonstrates the isolation technique (renaming `main` away) that this subtest omits. I grepped the whole tree for other coverage of mergeRefBaseTip / merge-ref fixtures (only scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:507-514 matched; other scripts/test/*.mjs files are unrelated), so the merge-ref-first-parent path has no assertion that discriminates it from the fallback. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a new code path shipped with a test named for it that cannot fail when that path is broken.

verdict.reason: The push arm of resolveRefs (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:299-307) resolves head as `verified(payload.after) ?? "HEAD"`, and nothing in the repository exercises it. The only push-related test (scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:223-228) calls `resolve` with GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push and GITHUB_REF_NAME=main, which returns FULL at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:530 before resolveRefs is ever reached (called at line 545). Every other GITHUB_EVENT_NAME in that test file is pull_request, merge_group, or schedule (lines 243, 250, 474, 574, 594, 608, 634). I widened the search beyond the reviewer's: repo-wide, only scripts/changed-areas.mjs and scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs mention GITHUB_EVENT_PATH at all, and only those two (plus docs) mention resolveRefs, so no other module — including scripts/test/verify-self-lanes.test.mjs and scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs, whose only "push" hits are Array.prototype.push — can construct a push payload or invoke the function indirectly. Consequently the new `after` resolution, the silent "HEAD" fallback when `after` is absent/unfetched, and the all-zeroes guard on the new {base, head} shape are all uncovered. That is a changed behavior with no meaningful test, which is a major issue under the test-adequacy rubric.
